correctness.rationale: Condition on the first Haar unitary row x: squared moduli P_j have the Dirichlet(1,...,1) distribution. The second row is uniform in x-perp, so the squared normalized inner product with z=(Lambda-mu I)x has Beta(1,d-2) law conditionally independent of x; for d=2 it is identically 1. The norm of z squared is the nonnegative Dirichlet spectral variance. For two-level eigenvalues, the aggregate Dirichlet mass X is Beta(k,d-k), and beta moments give the stated all-s>0 formula. Multiplying the s=1 entry moment by d(d-1) gives the exact projector mean coherence; gamma-ratio asymptotics separately cover fixed k, k/d→alpha in (0,1), and fixed corank m. Scalar spectra/Delta=0 and d=2 cases are handled correctly. The variance second-moment identity [d*tr(Lambda^2)-(tr Lambda)^2]/[d(d^2-1)] follows independently.

originality.rationale: Standard Haar row Dirichlet distributions and random projection matrix beta laws are existing theory; the claimed explicit independent conditional Beta factorization is a clean finite-dimensional specialization with evaluated all-rank l1-coherence gamma law and three distinct regimes. Cheng and Hall Sec. IV.A derive Haar-average purity bounds rather than this exact fixed-spectrum formula; their accessible full text explicitly discusses inability to evaluate the general l1 mean analytically. Pure-state coherence and relative-entropy coherence papers cover distinct observables and/or k=1 only. A classical Jacobi/orbital-corner identity might imply the scalar marginal after evaluation, leaving genuine overlap risk, but no decisive prior full claim was located.
residual_risks: Classical matrix-beta/Jacobi ensembles and orbital-corner distributions could imply the exact marginal indirectly after nontrivial integration.
Only l1 mean and entry moments, not variance or concentration of full coherence, are proved.

value.rationale: Mean l1-coherence of a Haar-rotated rank-k maximally mixed state is a natural basis-dependent quantum information invariant; exact finite-dimensional evaluation, all off-diagonal absolute moments, and the transition from linear to square-root to bounded growth across rank regimes answer motivated spectral-orbit questions beyond a mere normalization identity.

limitations: Complex Haar U(d) only, not real O(d).
For arbitrary eigenvalues the Dirichlet residual expectation is not necessarily elementary; two-level closed gamma expressions only.
residual_risks: Classical matrix-beta/Jacobi ensembles and orbital-corner distributions could imply the exact marginal indirectly after nontrivial integration.
Only l1 mean and entry moments, not variance or concentration of full coherence, are proved.
